newsitem.title: UK: Mobile phones can be pain in the neck - official.
newsitem.headline: Mobile phones can be pain in the neck - official.

text.p: Mobile phones can be a real pain, a British medical journal reported on Thursday.
A 49-year-old man who cradled a mobile phone in the crook of his neck while driving developed severe muscle weakness and pain in his arm and shoulder, his doctor, Anthony Hopkins, said.
The pain took a month to clear. During this time the man could not put his hand in his jacket pocket, Hopkins reported in the Journal of Neurology, Neurosurgery and Psychiatry.
"The symptoms were caused by compression of the upper shoulder nerve by the hard edge of the phone," the journal said.
